dialect.guess: GnuCOBOL (with DB2 embedded SQL, also compatible with IBM Enterprise COBOL on z/OS)
evidence: EXEC SQL ... END-EXEC blocks (DB2 embedded SQL)
EXEC SQL CONNECT RESET END-EXEC (GnuCOBOL DB2 connection pattern)
Comments explicitly mention GnuCOBOL and ZOS differences
COPY WSFST / COPY WSDT with REPLACING (copybook references)
RECORDING MODE IS F (IBM-style FD clause)

purpose.summary: This program reads all employee records from a DB2 view (VEMP) using a cursor and produces a formatted printed report with page headers, column headers, detail lines, and a footer showing total record count. It handles DB2 connection setup (including GnuCOBOL-specific connection logic) and cursor open/fetch/close lifecycle.

notable_features: EXEC SQL embedded DB2 (DECLARE CURSOR, OPEN, FETCH, CLOSE, CONNECT RESET)
SQLCA included via EXEC SQL INCLUDE SQLCA
COMP-5 for SQL status field (GnuCOBOL/Micro Focus binary)
Sequential file output for printed report with pagination logic
COPY statements with REPLACING for reusable working-storage snippets (WSFST, WSDT)
Explicit GnuCOBOL vs z/OS DB2 connection differences documented in comments
88-level condition names for SQL status codes including negative value (-803)
verdict.notes: The program is explicitly described as a learning/tutorial example ('Created to learn') by the author. It is part of a series (DBCBEX16 = DB COBOL Example 1-6). The COPY statements reference external copybooks (WSFST, WSDT) not shown in the source. The 9816-Create-Cursor-DB1 paragraph is effectively empty (commented-out debug display), which is intentional for this example. Minor typo in EOJ message: 'DCBCEX16' instead of 'DBCBEX16'.
